title: Microsoft Edge: view sensitivity labels on MIP protected PDFs in the new PDF viewer
summary: Pass with minor corrections: the documented PDF-reader policy and registry setting are accurate, and the briefing correctly reports the roadmap and release notes together. Microsoft's PDF-partnership announcement gives a different legacy-engine retirement schedule, and two checklist controls have no table row. The previous verifier comment's correction instructions were ignored and its findings checked independently.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans support for viewing the sensitivity label applied to a MIP protected PDF in Edge.
claims.quote: Enterprise customers can view sensitivity labels applied to MIP protected PDF

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on 2026-10-05T23:03:05.
The Stable channel release notes document the feature under version 138.0.3351.55, dated June 26, 2025.
claims.quote:
Version 138.0.3351.55: June 26, 2025
Adding support for viewing Sensitivity labels applied to a Microsoft Information Protection (MIP) Protected PDF

claims.claim: The Stable channel release notes describe label viewing as available in the new built-in PDF reader.
claims.quote: Enterprise customers can view sensitivity labels applied to MIP protected PDF to be well informed of the data classification to enable them to handle such sensitive documents. This change is available in the new Microsoft Edge built-in PDF reader.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The release notes describe a controlled feature rollout, so the feature might not yet be visible on every device.
claims.quote: Note: This is a controlled feature rollout. If you don't see this feature, check back as we continue our rollout.

claims.claim: Edge can view MIP protected files saved locally or in the cloud.
claims.quote: With Microsoft Edge, users can view MIP protected files saved locally, or in the cloud.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: A protected file opens in Edge if the signed-in profile has at least view permissions.
claims.quote: If the profile that the user is logged into Microsoft Edge with has at least view permissions to the file, the file will open in Microsoft Edge.

claims.claim: NewPDFReaderEnabled controls selection of the new built-in PDF reader powered by Adobe Acrobat's rendering engine.
claims.quote: The policy lets Microsoft Edge launch the new version of the built-in PDF reader that's powered by Adobe Acrobat's PDF rendering engine.

claims.claim: The policy is under Group Policy (ADMX), Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > Microsoft Edge built-in PDF reader powered by Adobe Acrobat enabled (deprecated).
claims.quote:
Group Policy (ADMX) info
GP name: Microsoft Edge built-in PDF reader powered by Adobe Acrobat enabled (deprecated)
GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge

claims.claim: The policy has the registry path SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge, value NewPDFReaderEnabled, type REG_DWORD.
claims.quote:
Registry settings
Path (Mandatory): SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge
Value name: NewPDFReaderEnabled
Value type: REG_DWORD

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: NewPDFReaderEnabled is deprecated starting in Edge 156.
claims.quote: Starting in Microsoft Edge version 156, this policy is deprecated as the built-in PDF reader experience has transitioned to the newer version.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The policy reference plans NewPDFReaderEnabled obsolescence starting in Edge 162.
claims.quote: The policy will remain supported for a minimum of 6 major releases and is planned to become obsolete starting in Microsoft Edge version 162.
claims.fix: Keep the Edge 162 plan explicitly attributed to the policy reference. Add: "Microsoft's September 2026 PDF-partnership FAQ instead says: 'The PDF engine in the Microsoft Edge built-in PDF reader is scheduled to be removed in Edge version 156.'" Cite https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoftedgeinsider/microsoft-edge-and-adobe-partner-to-improve-the-pdf-experience/3733481.

claims.claim: Once the policy becomes obsolete, organisations can no longer use it to opt out of the new PDF reader.
claims.quote: Once obsolete, organizations will no longer be able to use this policy to opt out of the new PDF reader.

claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly state that NewPDFReaderEnabled governs sensitivity-label display.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge new PDF reader Adobe Acrobat sensitivity labels NewPDFReaderEnabled macOS government; read NewPDFReaderEnabled, Edge PDF reader, Stable 138 release notes and Edge policies. Reader selection is documented, not a specific label-display policy.
